attributes.body_ja:
「とは」は、文末（ぶんまつ）でよく使（つか）われる強調表現（きょうちょうひょうげん）で、直前（ちょくぜん）の内容（ないよう）が話（はな）し手（て）にとって衝撃的（しょうげきてき）・意外（いがい）・予想外（よそうがい）であることを示（しめ）します。「とは」を使（つか）うことで、具体的（ぐたいてき）な感情（かんじょう）を言（い）わなくても、話（はな）し手（て）が強（つよ）い気持（きも）ちを抱（いだ）いていることを表現（ひょうげん）することができます。

「とは」は、引用（いんよう）の格助詞（かくじょし）「と」と主題（しゅだい）を示（しめ）す副助詞（ふくじょし）「は」の組（く）み合（あ）わせです。この表現（ひょうげん）は、(A) について特（とく）に何（なに）か言（い）わなくても、それを主題（しゅだい）として取（と）り上（あ）げ、強調（きょうちょう）する働（はたら）きを持（も）ちます。

「とは」は、「など」のような言葉（ことば）の後（あと）に置（お）かれることもあります。 この場合（ばあい）も、話（はな）し手（て）が「(A) など」に対（たい）して強（つよ）い驚（おどろ）きや衝撃（しょうげき）を感（かん）じていることを表（あらわ）しています。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「とは」は、感情（かんじょう）を表（あらわ）す語（ご）が省（はぶ）かれた文（ぶん）の最後（さいご）で使（つか）われるのが一般的（いっぱんてき）ですが、「とは」の後（あと）で話（はな）し手（て）が自分（じぶん）の感情（かんじょう）をはっきりと述（の）べることもあります。
attributes.body:
とは is an emphatic structure that is regularly seen at the end of sentences, and will imply that the statement before it is shocking, appalling, or unexpected. In English, it translates very similarly as 'to think that (A)' in that it expresses a strong emotional response without expressly saying what that exact response is.

とは is a combination of the case-marking particle と in its quotation use, and the adverbial particle は. In this way, it is just marking the whole statement of (A) as what is being highlighted as the topic, without actually stating anything else about it.

とは may sometimes be seen following など or similar structures, and in these cases will just imply that 'something like (A)' is what is shocking.

Caution

Although it is common for とは to come at the end of a sentence with the actual feeling word omitted, the speaker may expressly state their reaction afterwards.

なんて can overlap in meaning with とは when used in phrases like 優勝できる（とは）・（なんて）夢にも思わなかった ('Never even in my dreams did I think we could win the championship.'). なんて however has a variety of usages that do not apply to とは, such as to comment (often negatively) on 'things like (A)', e.g. 嘘なんて大嫌い ('I hate things like lies.').

attributes.body: Both expressions can be used to convey shock and surprise, though how they function in a sentence differs. まさか precedes whatever the speaker is surprised about, e.g. まさか勝てるなんて ('To think they could win!'), or even on its own as an interjection, i.e. まさか！ ('No way!). In contrast, とは always follows what the speaker is surprised about, and can pair with まさか for further emphasis, e.g. まさか勝てるとは (same meaning as the above example).

second_relatable.title: まさか
second_relatable.meaning: I never dreamed, Never, No way, Don't tell me, You don't say

attributes.body: まさか and とは are both used to express surprise, but function in different ways. まさか comes at the beginning of a sentence to emphasize that what follows goes against the speaker's expectations, while とは appears at the end of a sentence or phrase to express the same. Because they occupy different positions, they are often used together. For example, まさか勝てるとは！ ('To think we could win!' / 'I never thought we could win').
